name: Visteon Corp
business: Designs and manufactures cockpit electronics (digital clusters, displays, infotainment, domain controllers, battery management) for global automakers.

events.what: No CEO or CFO change in window. Own 8-K Item 5.02 query (2024-07-01 to 2026-10-02) shows only two director elections and 2025 pay amendments. Sachin Lawande CEO since 2015-06-29 (contract extended to 2030-09-30); Jerome Rouquet CFO since 2020-03-01. No 'first earnings call' or 'since joining' language in 2026 calls.

Investor Day: 2029 framework (high single-digit sales growth, 14.1% EBITDA margin by 2029, about $1 billion cumulative FCF 2026 to 2029, about $1 billion returned, new $800 million buyback authorization)
$200 million accelerated share repurchase announced; $20 million engineering services tuck-in closed in June 2026 (no Item 1.01/2.01 8-K in window)

next_event.source: Investor Day already held 2026-06-25 (document_id 48340); no further framework event found. Next touchpoint is the Q3 2026 earnings call (date not in corpus) and 2027 guidance with Q4.

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Same metric for target and consensus (adjusted EBITDA). 2026 guide $455 million to $495 million, about 12.8% at midpoint. CFO flagged about 100 bps of memory-inflation headwind in 2027 before expansion in 2028 and 2029. Baba FY labels equal company fiscal years (December FYE).

statements.quote: Turning now to profitability. We're targeting an EBITDA margin of 14.1% by 2029, with steady expansion over the period.
statements.speaker: Jerome Rouquet

statements.quote: From a phasing standpoint, 2027 includes an incremental headwind from memory inflation of approximately 100 basis points of margin. This is compounded by the rollout of legacy recoveries and the non-recurrence of certain 2026 one-time items. Margin expands more meaningfully in 2028 and 2029, supported by volume growth, easing inflation, and operational efficiencies.
statements.speaker: Jerome Rouquet

statements.quote: We're targeting high single-digit sales growth, continued margin expansion to over 14%, and cumulative free cash flow generation of approximately $1 billion over the period.
statements.speaker: Jerome Rouquet

statements.quote: With regards to adjusted EBITDA, we continue to expect between $455 million and $495 million and are trending towards the midpoint of the range of approximately $475 million.
statements.speaker: Jerome Rouquet

street.gap_assumption: Same metric (adjusted EBITDA). FY2029 consensus $650.2 million EBITDA on $4,658 million revenue = 13.96% vs 14.1% target. The street already models the Investor Day path, including a flat 2027.
street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (Visible Alpha), data_comps revisions asof 2026-10-01

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [Q1 2026, Q2 2026]. Q1 from VA actuals; Q2 2026 from CFO on call (sales $960 million, adjusted EBITDA $116 million, document_id 81949), not yet in VA actuals. Compression from memory and semiconductor cost inflation with recoveries lagging; Q2 was best margin since Q3 2025. LTM 11.9% is Q3 2025 to Q2 2026.

disqualifier_reason: Margin target already reflected in consensus: FY2029 consensus EBITDA margin 13.96% vs management's 14.1% target (14 bps gap, 1.0% EBITDA uplift). Also no leadership change: CEO since 2015, CFO since 2020; the only in-window catalyst is the June 2026 Investor Day by the same team.
verdict: Not the archetype: very cheap at about 4x EBITDA and down 36%, with a dated 14.1% 2029 margin target, but the street already models it and leadership is unchanged.
open_questions: Can Visteon recover memory cost inflation fast enough that 2027 is not the flat year consensus (12.51%) assumes?
Does the $1 billion 2026 to 2029 capital return, about 40% of the market cap, matter more than the margin path?
Is customer concentration (Ford 26% of 2025 sales) a structural cap on margin?
